answer: Sybil resistance comes from requiring every identity to complete a fresh chain of sequential modular squarings before it is accepted. A Wesolowski proof lets peers verify the result efficiently, but GPUs cannot shortcut the dependency within one chain; cloning identities therefore requires more independent hardware and elapsed time, not merely more parallel threads. A juniper beacon can mark the challenge epoch, while each vertex-bound identity remains gated by its own completed delay.
